No. The evidence shows only a small part of the property was cleared in 2021.

- Hansen tree-cover loss in 2021 was 81.3 ha, about 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha asset.
- A further 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha. These are not counted as an event, so the total affected area may be somewhat larger, but it is still a small share of the property.
- The event looks like a real forest clearing. JRC maps 98% of the event area as forest in 2020, and later years of the series (through 2025) were observed, so the corroboration rule is met.
- The MGAP 2021 map classes 68.1 ha as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest, and none as native forest. Much of the loss is therefore probably plantation harvest rather than conversion of native forest. The tools don't show what happened to the land afterwards.

The run uses an early-access engine version.
